page: Hetzner Cloud cax11 is an entry-level ARM-based virtual machine within the provider's Cost Optimized family. Running on a QEMU hypervisor, the instance is allocated 2 shared vCPUs derived from Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 physical processors operating at 2.0 GHz. The compute setup is paired with 4.0 GB of system memory (1.95 GB per core) and includes 40 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. There are no dedicated graphics processing units attached.

Benchmark evaluations place the processing capability predominantly in the entry-tier brackets. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU throughput registers in the average range, whereas multi-core execution falls into the bottom 25 percent. Across synthetic suites like Geekbench and PassMark, multi-core, ray tracing, image processing, and memory bandwidth tests consistently show poor to weak metrics compared to larger server classes. In practical application tests, the instance records 2.47 million operations per second in Redis SET routines and 2.11 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

Because the cax11 relies on shared vCPUs, sustained compute performance can be subject to resource contention from neighbor workloads. However, the 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, integrated NVMe disk, and power-efficient ARM architecture deliver strong qualitative cost efficiency for resource-light footprints that do not require dedicated x86 instructions or sustained maximum CPU utilization.

The server profile is primarily fit for small auxiliary tasks, including lightweight web serving, staging environments, low-throughput microservices, edge proxies, and developmental ARM build pipelines. It is unsuited for memory-intensive caching, heavy compilation jobs, database clustering, or dense machine learning workloads.
description: Hetzner Cloud cax11 is a cost-optimized, ARM-based cloud server equipped with 2 shared vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. Designed for entry-level deployments, the configuration provides 4.0 GB of memory alongside 40 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, with no integrated hardware accelerators. Synthetic performance metrics reflect its resource footprint: stress-ng single-core processing demonstrates moderate throughput, while multi-core computation, Geekbench results, and memory subsystem bandwidth score in the lower percentiles relative to standard cloud infrastructure. Application testing shows 2.47 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 2.11 GB/sec static web throughput. Given the shared CPU allocation and modest memory headroom, the cax11 represents an economical choice for non-critical services, small development or staging nodes, basic container hosting, and light web servers.
